title: A wondrous recitation
hookLine: a group of jinn listened and said, we've heard a wondrous recitation (72:1–2)
carry: it guides to what is right

cards: Dawn, in a valley on the road to the market of 'Ukaz. A small group of travelers stop to pray, and one of them leads, reciting aloud. Nobody else is around, as far as they know.
But someone is listening: a group of beings who had come searching for something else entirely, who stop, gather close, and hear the words to the end.
Then they go home to their people and say: we've heard something wondrous. Surah seventy-two is named for them. Al-Jinn.

teach.h: SAY: IT WAS REVEALED TO ME.
teach.b: The surah begins with an instruction to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: say, it has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened. And they said, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! we have heard a marvellous Qur'an."
Marvelous is 'ajab in Arabic: wondrous, astonishing, something that makes you stop. Qur'an here means what it literally means: a recitation.

The jinn, in Islamic belief, are real beings, created from smokeless fire, unseen by us, with free will like humans. Some believe, some don't. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Ibn 'Abbas, tells the setting.
The jinn had noticed the sky had changed; they were being driven back from listening at the heavens, so they spread out across the earth to find out why.
One group came upon the Prophet and his companions at a place called Nakhlah, praying the dawn prayer. They heard the recitation and said: this is what has come between us and the sky.
One surprising detail: the verse says it was revealed to me that they listened.
In Ibn 'Abbas's account, the Prophet didn't see them that morning; he learned about his audience afterward, through revelation.
Then the jinn went back to their people, verse two: it guides to what is right, so we believe in it, and we will not set up anyone as partner to our Lord. Their response wasn't fear. It was wonder.
They came looking for an explanation and found a recitation, and in verse two it's the recitation itself, guiding to what is right, that they say won them over.

how: Muslims count the jinn among unseen beings with free will; surah al-Jinn and 46:29–32 tell of jinn who heard the Qur'an and believed, and listening to recitation is a devotional practice in its own right.

o: wondrous, astonishing enough to make you stop
frightening, a sound that makes you run
strange and foreign, hard to understand

games.q: a wondrous recitation — tap the pairs.
p: unseen beings made from smokeless fire
where they heard the dawn prayer

s: the Prophet saw the jinn listening that dawn
the surah says it was revealed to him; Ibn 'Abbas says he didn't see them.
the jinn came looking for why the sky had changed
they were searching, and found the recitation.
the jinn's first response was fear
it was wonder: we have heard a marvelous recitation.

games.q: you're one of the jinn. you came searching for why the sky changed, and you hear a man reciting at dawn. what do you do?
o: listen to the end, then tell your people.
games.why: they listened, went back, and said: we have heard a marvelous recitation that guides to what is right, so we believe.

practice: If you can, play a recitation of the Qur'an quietly, any reciter, any surah, and just listen, even if you don't understand the Arabic.
If you'd rather not, close your eyes and listen to whatever is around you, traffic, wind, your own breath, as if you'd never heard it before. Notice the moment something sounds new.

wordCard.voice: 'Ajab. In 72:1 a group of jinn hear the Qur'an at dawn and call it wondrous, 'ajab, astonishing enough to make them stop and listen. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, 72:1: a wondrous recitation. qur'an, recitation; 'ajab, wonder.

carryVoice: Your line: it guides to what is right. They came for an answer and found wonder. That's day six hundred fifty.
